MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 28, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on November 28, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 22, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:50 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel -- Anticipated Litigation. Significant exposure to
  litigation pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 54956.9: one case. Initiation of
  litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: one case.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City

City Council Minutes  1  November 28, 2017
 Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present (Council Member
Raths arrived during Closed Session at 5:50 p.m.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council focused on the potential initiation of
litigation and the threat of litigation from the law firm that is asserting the City is violating the
California Voting Rights Act by holding at-large elections. Regarding the initiation of litigation,
Mr. Curley said his office has taken the lead and drafted an Amicus Brief in support of a Federal
case that has been filed; Higginson vs. the City of Poway and the State of California. That action
is seeking injunctive and permanent relief in declaring the California Voting Rights Act
unconstitutional for a variety of reasons. Mr. Curley noted that he has been asked to lead the effort
with this multi-state action and the oral arguments are set for January, however there have been
motions made to move the date up sooner. For the second component, the City Council further
discussed the threat of litigation from Shenkman and Hughes. Mr. Curley said he wants to make
sure that it is clear that no decision has been made. The City is in a time period called a “safe
harbor” which makes it immune to litigation and the Council and community have the opportunity
to assess the circumstances pursuant to a statutory framework. After all the evidence is seen, the
City Council can decide if they will move to district elections or not. Mr. Curley announced that
the second public hearing will occur tonight, without mapping involved however beginning
tomorrow, anyone is welcome to submit mapping ideas for dividing the city into five equal areas.
Anything submitted will be considered and analyzed and precise calendaring for future meetings
is forthcoming. Mr. Curley invited the public to participate in this process and to provide input. In
closing, Mr. Curley outlined costs and said the defense of these lawsuits is generally $500,000 to
$1 million. He said it has been well noted that no California city has prevailed because of the low
bar and the City of Palmdale had to pay $4.5 million. The lower range is zero to $30,000 if a city
stays in the safe harbor, with an upper range in the millions. He said there is a lot of public money
at stake and that is why the City is seeking strong public participation.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Mission Viejo Football Coach Bob Johnson as a "Home Town Hero"

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that it is impossible to imagine Bob Johsnon not being out on
  the Mission Viejo High School football field. She said he positively impacted thousands
  of student athletes and she wished him well in his retirement.

  Mayor Bucknum presented Coach Johnson with the Hometown Hero proclamation.

P2.  Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control District Presentation

City Council Minutes  2  November 28, 2017
   Vector Control District Board Member Dave Leckness made the presentation and noted
  that there has been a decline of mosquito infestation in Mission Viejo over the last 18
  months.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following expressed concern with the City’s use of the herbicide glyphosate. They asked the
Council to form a “Non-Toxic Mission Viejo” committee to talk about the impacts of these
chemicals and to explore ways to discontinue use of these products: James Marin (no city of
residence listed); Natalie Paffrath, M.V.; Felissa Silva, M.V.; Zen Honeycutt, M.V.; Michael
Rotcher, M.V.; and Lisa Germo, Sun City.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: reminded the Council that a former Council Member believed that the position
on the Vector Control Board of Directors should be held by a sitting Council Member, not a
resident. She noted, however, that a resident is currently serving on the Vector Board and the next
time the spot is open for appointment, she would like the opportunity to apply.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of November 14, 2017, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated November 3, 2017 in the Amount of $839,926.12

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated November 10, 2017 in the Amount of $3,040,761.46

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - First Quarter 2017-18

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  November 28, 2017
 5.  Purchase of Network and Wireless Hardware for Marguerite Recreation Center

  Approved entering into agreement for professional services and issuance of purchase order
  for network hardware to Resilient Communications for $70,502.20 including a 10% project
  contingency.

6.  Library Automated System Software and Hardware Support Agreement

  Approved issuance of a purchase order in the amount of $69,826.78 for maintenance and
  support of the Library automated systems software and hardware agreement with
  SirsiDynix, Inc.

7.  Library Holiday Schedule for 2018 Calendar Year

  Approved proposed Library Holiday and Closure Schedule for 2018.

8.  Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 17837)

  Approved the plans and specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids for the
  Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 17837) project.

9.  Marguerite Fiber Expansion Project

  Authorized staff to enter into agreement and issue a purchase order to PacifiCom, Inc., for
  an amount not to exceed $71,349.73 including 10% project contingency.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARINGS

10.  Overview of the California Voting Rights Act and Request for Public Input

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 7:28 p.m., Mayor Bucknum opened the public hearing.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: volunteered to be on a committee on this topic and expressed concern
  that two senior communities might fall in the same district.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that the City's outreach has been poor and that maps should be
  placed in the lobby for people to take home and study. She said the City should reach out to
  the homeowners associations and have a clearer link to the districting information from the
  website’s home page.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: stated that in Mission Viejo, minorities are disbursed evenly throughout
  the City and he is opposed to changing to district based elections. He offered his volunteer
  legal services to the City Attorney to challenge the matter.
City Council Minutes  4  November 28, 2017
   Bob Ollry, M.V.: said that he has never seen a more racially integrated city and that the threat
  of litigation is a shakedown by two attorneys in Malibu who have no business telling Mission
  Viejo how to run the city.

  Dennis O'Connor: stated that he is undecided on this topic and he shared some of his
  observations, both pro and con, for district elections.

  Bob Ruesch, M.V.: expressed concern that the City is being forced to take the path of district
  representation and he wondered if residents would get the best people representing the City
  or the best people representing the district. He said that he humbly asks the City Council to
  look at fighting this.

  Mayor Bucknum closed the public hearing at 7:50 p.m.

  By consensus, the City Council authorized the City Manager/City Attorney to spend up to
  $100,000 to immediately begin investigating the City’s past elections in order to evaluate the
  claim of racially polarized elections.

  City Attorney Curley announced that this matter will be heard again at the City Council
  Meeting of December 12, 2017.

OLD BUSINESS

11.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Contract Law Enforcement Cost and
  Efficiency Study

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to award a
  contract to Matrix Consulting Group in the amount of $269,500.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

12.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
City Council Minutes  5  November 28, 2017
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that his first grandchild, a girl named Cambria, was born
yesterday and he is very excited to be a grandparent.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley congratulated Council Member Goodell on becoming a granddad. She
said she took three of her eight grandkids to the Santa's Arrival celebration and she thanked the
Mission Viejo Activities Committee for a wonderful event. She reminded residents that Santa and
Mrs. Claus will be in their workshop from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. every Wednesday, Saturday and
Sunday through December 20, 2017. Council Member Kelley announced that she attended the Carl
Hankey Hawk Trot which was a fundraiser for the school’s International Baccalaureate (IB)
program. She noted that Hankey school is quite unique as it is the only public school with an IB
program between Long Beach and San Diego. She said that earlier today she was pleased to visit
Esperanza School to celebrate Giving Tuesday and to thank the students for making blankets for
the animals at the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center. Council Member Kelley announced that
she will not be present at the next meeting on December 12, however, she will be present by
telephone which the City Clerk and City Attorney said is achievable.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths noted that he is a member of the Mission Viejo Rotary Club which meets
for breakfast on Wednesday mornings at the Mission Viejo Country Club so they can plan events
that help the community. He said tomorrow’s meeting will be a change of venue and will be held
at World Class Pizza where they’ll have free pizza and an open invitation for the community to
attend starting at 5:00 p.m. Council Member Raths thanked the Orange County Sheriff’s
Department deputies for all they do for the City and the county. He said they are in the trenches
every day and do an amazing job. Council Member Raths mentioned that on Thanksgiving, a 2
year-old fell in a pool and luckily an 8 year-old saw it happen and the child's life was saved. He
said it could have been a disastrous Thanksgiving for the family and he mentioned it to provide a
reminder that drownings happen all year long and people need to teach their children to swim.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs announced that several people have approached him recently to comment
about the great holiday train display at the Civic Center. He said he wanted to emphasize that who
a person votes for, at all levels of government, is very important as it has a great impact on
municipalities. He noted that prevailing wage and minimum wage laws continue to escalate and
the City of Mission Viejo can do nothing about it. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said that the California
Civil Rights Act, which was passed by legislators and signed by the Governor, comes full circle
City Council Minutes  6  November 28, 2017
 to this point. Referring to the public speakers earlier in the evening, Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said he
was moved by the folks who talked about a non-toxic Mission Viejo. He feels that the community
should be engaged in this topic along with the water districts. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked what
chemicals the City is using and what steps staff is taking to protect the public.

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay stated that those who apply the
chemicals are licensed and the City’s contractors use glyphosate in very limited areas. It is only
used in the medians and not on sidewalks or at parks.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked Director Rattay to meet with the group of people that spoke this
evening and he thanked him for the proactive approach. He also said he was distraught to hear one
resident talk about the amount of chemicals in her tap water and he feels that the water districts
need to understand this and be part of the cleanup. In conclusion, Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said he is
glad that Council Member Kelley will be available by telephone at the December 12 meeting.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum announced that all of the Council Members want the right thing to be done and
for the City to be proactive about glyphosate and the treatment of grass, sports fields, roadways
and Oso Creek. She asked Assistant City Manager Rattay to come back with information on how
the creek water is tested. Mayor Bucknum reiterated the positive sentiments about the Santa's
arrival celebration and said she noticed new groups and activities this year including the folks that
paint decorative kindness message on rocks and place them around town and three students who
won the opportunity to read The Night Before Christmas with her. Mayor Bucknum discussed her
attendance at the Gifts and Goodies Boutique where she did a lot of Christmas shopping with local
vendors and she encouraged residents to think about shopping locally and keeping tax dollars in
town. She said if people shop online and choose store delivery, the tax dollars come to Mission
Viejo. She also discussed her attendance at the Turning Red Tape into Red Carpet awards
ceremony and Second Harvest Food Bank’s No Lunch Lunch which raised funds and food for
those that are less fortunate. Mayor Bucknum noted that there is a lot going on around the City and
she looks forward to seeing residents around town during the holiday festivities. She ended her
comments with a special prayer for former City Commissioner Ron Ruef's son who is having
difficulty getting out of Bali after the volcano eruption in that country.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:34 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, December 12, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of December 12, 2017
